Step: Double-click SOC Debating & MUN on the desktop.
In the staff window, sign in as coordinator.
The private window is your student laptop.
Keep the two windows side by side.
People → Year 9 Model UN (demo).
Open the sign-in cards and use print preview (Ctrl + P).
Show one student's code. In the student window, type it at /join.
Type a wrong code five times in a row.
Staff window: Manage → New code for that student. Student window: reload.
Sign the student in again with the new code.
Student: Prepare.
Chair → Open a session for the committee. Open the Projector link in a third window.
Run roll call. The student answers on their screen.
Agenda, then opening statements: add the student's country to the speakers list, start the timer, give that student extra time.
The floor: the student raises a point and proposes a motion (unmoderated caucus, 5 min). Chair seconds and passes it.
Student: draft an amendment to one operative paragraph, then submit it.
Chair: sign it with other delegations if needed, Bring to the floor, Vote on the amendment. The student votes.
Close debate, then into voting procedure. Start the whip count: the student predicts how named delegations will vote.
Vote on the whole resolution. Close the vote.
Open the debrief (chair and student).
Minutes: edit a line, then download as Word. Open it in Word.
MUN → committee → Prediction for a paragraph.
Create lobbying tasks from the swing list. Check the student sees their task.
Repeat B.9 quickly in the Security Council (demo), with a permanent member voting no.
Debating → New class debate. Pick the Year 8 Debating class, a motion, and Fill empty places from the class list. Set it up.
Open the projector view. Use Space, → and ← to run two speeches.
Score each speaker, add a comment, choose the winner.
Sign the student window in as one of those Year 8 students.
Debating → New speaking round → Impromptu, the whole class in random order. Run one turn.
Start a debate case: a motion and a side, plus one argument in four parts.
Rebuttal: answer one of the three likely arguments.
Speeches: pick a template; check the word count and cue cards.
Practise a speech: an impromptu drill. Score yourself and save.
Staff window: Debating → Student preparation. Find that work and leave a comment.
During a live session, close the black window. Wait 10 seconds, then start it again.
Refresh the chair console mid-vote.
Make a change, then press Undo.
Delete something from an Admin table, then restore it ("Show deleted").
Student window: do B.3 to B.7 with the keyboard only (Tab, Enter, Space).
Zoom the student window to 200% (Ctrl + +).
Footer → Easy-read text.
If NVDA is installed: listen to one live student page.
